quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 (January-December 2025) results, non-GAAP: revenue JPY 13,185 hundred million, down 2.2% (FY2024: JPY 13,485 hundred million) - Industrial/Infrastructure/IoT revenue rose on higher demand in the infrastructure business while Automotive revenue fell on market softening; gross profit JPY 7,599 hundred million, gross margin 57.6% (+1.6pts, lower manufacturing costs offsetting lower Automotive sales and factory utilization); operating profit JPY 3,869 hundred million, operating margin 29.3% (-0.2pt, higher SG&A). IFRS: revenue JPY 13,212 hundred million (-2.0%), operating profit JPY 2,012 hundred million (15.2% margin). The company booked a pre-tax loss of JPY 303 hundred million; the year included a JPY 236,600 million loss (including currency effects, recorded in finance costs) on its Wolfspeed deposit, converted into other financial assets under the restructuring support agreement after Wolfspeed's US Chapter 11 filing and restructuring plan.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 non-GAAP revenue JPY 13,185 hundred million (-2.2%); GM 57.6%; OP JPY 3,869 hundred million (29.3%); Wolfspeed-related loss JPY 236,600 million

quarterly_data.signal: Company targets and strategy: the mid-term financial model (non-GAAP, at fixed rates of USD 1 = JPY 100 and EUR 1 = JPY 120) targets a 55% gross margin and a 25-30% operating margin, plus revenue growth above the market; at the June 25, 2025 Capital Markets Day the operating-margin target was revised from 30% to a 25%-30% range, to create room to strengthen the organisation and finances for long-term growth. At those fixed rates FY2025 non-GAAP gross margin was about 55% and operating margin about 24%. Capex is to be kept at about 5% of revenue over the mid to long term. Under its Purposeful Investment policy the company prioritises three Secular Growth areas - SDV (software-defined vehicles), AI infrastructure/compute and Intelligence at the Edge. Management states that AI growth and a demand recovery in some areas are expected in the short term, but the business environment is expected to remain uncertain.
quarterly_data.figure: Targets: GM 55%, OPM 25-30% (USD 1 = JPY 100); capex about 5% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Capex and production: FY2025 capex (investment-decision basis) JPY 576 hundred million, mainly building a high-voltage MOSFET manufacturing line, consolidating design and development sites, renewing IT infrastructure and renewing production equipment; during the year the domestic fabs added equipment to raise supply capacity for some products in short supply and to improve resilience. The company continues to build a die bank and to secure and expand output at outsourced manufacturing partners. No full-year FY2026 capex plan is disclosed (quarterly guidance only); Q1 2026 capex (investment-decision basis) was planned at about JPY 850 hundred million, mainly for strengthening the manufacturing setup, renewing production equipment at each site and strengthening design and development.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 capex JPY 576 hundred million (high-voltage MOSFET line); Q1 2026 plan about JPY 850 hundred million

quarterly_data.signal: R&D result - GaN power for next-generation AI infrastructure: Renesas launched a high-voltage 650V GaN power semiconductor, the core of its GaN power solution, using its new Gen IV Plus process and the SuperGaN technology of Transphorm (acquired in 2024), with smaller die size and lower resistance than the previous generation and three thermally enhanced package options. The GaN power solution, aimed at next-generation AI infrastructure such as data centers (where the report notes the 800V DC power architecture is expected as a more efficient next-generation approach), covers 48V to 400V and scales to up to 800V by combining several devices; it can also serve EV charging, UPS, energy storage and solar inverters.
quarterly_data.figure: 650V GaN on Gen IV Plus; 48V-400V, scalable to 800V

quarterly_data.signal: R&D: FY2025 R&D spending (including capitalised development costs) JPY 2,403 hundred million, down from JPY 2,498 hundred million. Products from R&D: four RA8-series 32-bit MCUs on 22nm NVM technology with a 1 GHz CPU core - RA8P1 (AI acceleration and motor control), RA8T2 (motor control), RA8M2 (general purpose) and RA8D2 (graphics/HMI) - for Intelligence at the Edge.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 2,403 hundred million (FY2024: JPY 2,498 hundred million); RA8 MCUs at 22nm, 1 GHz

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio: in February 2026 Renesas agreed to sell its timing business to SiTime Corporation (definitive agreement signed by its US subsidiary on February 5, 2026), judging SiTime the best owner for the business's growth; completion was expected by the end of 2026 subject to regulatory approvals. The two companies also signed a memorandum to consider a partnership to develop new solutions integrating Renesas embedded compute technology with SiTime's MEMS timing technology at the silicon level.
quarterly_data.figure: Timing business sale to SiTime agreed February 5, 2026; MEMS timing integration MOU
